Stdlib ``unittest`` only, standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_f3d_webgl2_js.py

The file checks always run. The behavioural checks shell out to
``node -e`` snippets that load the sidecar against a MOCK WebGL2
context object which records every GL call; when ``node`` is not
on PATH they are SKIPPED LOUDLY via ``skipUnless``.

The mock is the headless proof: real GPU rasterization requires
a browser, so no test here claims pixel output -- only that the
sidecar issues the exact shader sources, buffer uploads,
uniform upload and draw call a real WebGL2 context would need,
and that projectPoint() matches Python-computed expectations
under the Fortran mat4 convention (column-major flat layout,
element (row, col) at m[col*4 + row], perspective divide when
|w| > 1e-12, mirroring mat4_transform_vec3 in src/math_3d.f90)
to within 1e-9.

reference-space fallback, stereo views, graceful degradation).

cases.src:
Parity coverage / stop-rule tests (seat B86, MASTER-PLAN section 3).

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_parity_coverage.py

This is the governance gate for the Feature-Parity Matrix
(MASTER-PLAN section 3, rows 1-36).  Waves continue until B86 reports
100 % ``Done-verified`` -- that is the stop rule.

Cross-check design (deliberate): seat B85 owns the parity generator
(``tools/parity_matrix.py``), ``docs/parity-status.json`` and the
generated ``docs/parity-matrix.json``.  This test does **not** import
or reuse B85's parser.  It parses the section 3 tables in
``docs/plan/MASTER-PLAN.md`` itself, from scratch, and checks B85's
artefacts against that independent reading -- a re-run of the same
code could not catch a parser bug shared by both sides.

Contracts checked:

* MASTER-PLAN section 3 contains exactly rows 1..36.
* ``docs/parity-status.json`` maps every row 1..36 to
  ``{"status": ..., "evidence": ...}`` where ``status`` is one of the
  allowed values only and ``evidence`` is a non-empty string.
* Every ``Done-verified`` row cites proof: its evidence names at
  least one test (contains "test", case-insensitively).
* Coverage (% of rows that are ``Done-verified``) is printed, and is
  >= the baseline recorded in ``parity-status.json`` under the
  top-level key ``_baseline_pct``.  A missing ``_baseline_pct`` key is
  a failure naming the key (the baseline is what stops coverage from
  silently regressing between waves).
* ``docs/parity-matrix.json`` exists and its row count matches the
  number of row entries in ``parity-status.json``.

cases.src:
Tests for Forge3D diagnostics (tools/f3dc/errors.py) and CLI check.

Stdlib unittest only; standalone-runnable:

    python3 tests/compiler/test_errors.py

Tests for the Forge3D Wave A lights/environment extension.

Covers ``tools/f3dc/ext_lights_env.py``: point/spot light extraction,
validation and ``.scene`` lines, plus scene fog / tonemap / shadow
extraction, validation and lines.

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_ext_lights_env.py

Tests for the Forge3D Wave A material extension (ext_materials.py).

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_ext_materials.py
    python3 -m unittest tests.compiler.test_ext_materials

Covers the Wave A surface: the ``standard`` material defaults
(metalness 0.0 / roughness 1.0), the phong ``specular`` / ``shininess``
defaults, range validation messages, PPM-only texture extraction and
validation, the exact ``objmat`` emit line, and ``apply_to_ir_object``.

Tests for the Forge3D Wave B deterministic-particles extension.

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_ext_particles.py
    python3 -m unittest tests.compiler.test_ext_particles

Covers the Wave B surface (MASTER-PLAN row 32): particle defaults,
named + hex + tuple colours, the exact ``particles`` emit line, the
validation errors, and the Python mirror of the frozen particle math
from ``src/particles.f90`` -- including the cross-language hash anchor
``hash01(1, 0, 0) == 0.5205930033698678`` hardcoded by Fortran seat
B71, and a state check whose expected value is computed in the test
directly from the frozen recipe (never via the module under test).

Tests for the Forge3D Wave B glTF extension (ext_gltf.py).

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_ext_gltf.py
    python3 -m unittest tests.compiler.test_ext_gltf

All fixtures are built in code (``struct`` / ``base64`` / ``json``)
and written to a fresh temporary directory per test.

Tests for the Forge3D Wave B keyframe-track extension.

Covers ``tools/f3dc/ext_keys.py``: building normalised tracks from
``keys`` headers + ``key`` dicts, validation, and ``.scene`` lines.

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_ext_keys.py

Tests for the Forge3D Wave B sprites + text extension.

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_ext_sprites_text.py
    python3 -m unittest tests.compiler.test_ext_sprites_text

Covers the Wave B surface: sprite / text defaults, named + hex +
tuple colours, the exact ``sprite`` / ``text`` emit lines, and the
validation errors (size range, finite coordinates, empty / over-long
text, unsupported characters).

Tests for the Forge3D Wave C orthographic-camera extension.

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_ext_cameras.py
    python3 -m unittest tests.compiler.test_ext_cameras

Covers the Wave C surface (MASTER-PLAN parity row 3): the frozen
syntax ``camera ortho [size N] [at x,y,z] [look x,y,z] [fov ignored]``,
the defaults (bare ``camera ortho`` -> size 5.0), explicit size,
at/look pass-through, invalid-size errors, perspective emitting no
lines, and the ``ortho SIZE`` line formatted with ``%.6g`` like the
other ``ext_*`` modules.

Tests for the Forge3D Wave C post-processing extension.

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_ext_post.py
    python3 -m unittest tests.compiler.test_ext_post

Covers the Wave C surface (MASTER-PLAN row 30): every filter's
frozen default, explicit amounts (dict props, token lists and
source-line strings), ordered chains via ``collect_post``, the exact
``post`` emit line and its ``%.6g`` formatting, and the validation
errors for unknown names and out-of-range amounts. Pixel math is out
of scope here by design (it lives in Fortran + JS).

Tests for the Forge3D Wave D geometry extension (seat D08).

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_ext_geometry.py
    python3 -m unittest tests.compiler.test_ext_geometry

Covers the ten Wave D primitives (circle, ring, capsule, tube,
lathe, extrude, icosahedron, octahedron, tetrahedron, dodecahedron,
torusknot): parse + validate + the frozen 20-token ``.scene``
object line (SIZE / RADIUS / HEIGHT / SEGMENTS at tokens 17-20,
point lists appended as tokens 21+), the exact triangle-estimate
formulas, the direct Fortran ``create_*`` calls, the defaults, and
the friendly error cases. Fortran geometry math is out of scope
here by design (it lives in the geo_*_3d modules).

Tests for the Forge3D Wave E custom-shader extension (compiler side).

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_ext_shader.py
    python3 -m unittest tests.compiler.test_ext_shader

Covers the frozen C2 surface: the expression tokeniser, the
shunting-yard compiler to RPN (precedence, associativity, parens,
unary minus, every function at its frozen arity), every error class
``to_rpn`` must raise on, ``validate_shader`` stack simulation, and
the exact ``shaderdef`` / ``shaderbind`` emit lines. Per-pixel
evaluation (and its semantics guards) is out of scope here by
design: it lives in Fortran + JS.

Tests for the Forge3D Wave E skinning + morph extension (C1).

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_ext_skin.py
    python3 -m unittest tests.compiler.test_ext_skin

Covers the frozen surface ``morph <target> <kind> <factor>`` /
``bone <name> [at x,y,z] [rotate rx,ry,rz] [radius r]`` /
``skin <target> <bonename>``: each validator's valid case and every
error case (unknown morph kind, factor out of range / not a number,
bad vec3 arity, radius <= 0, skin referencing an unknown bone,
duplicate bone name), the bone defaults filled in, and the exact
``scene_lines`` strings with ordering preserved. Per-vertex morph /
skinning math is out of scope here by design (it lives in Fortran +
JS).
Tests for the Forge3D lexer (tools/f3dc/lexer.py). Stdlib unittest only.

Programs are built through the real front end -- ``parser.parse`` feeds

Wave A compiler parity tests (seat B61, MASTER-PLAN section 3).

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_wavea_parity.py

Every test drives the real pipeline -- ``parser.parse`` ->
``validate.validate`` -> ``emit_fortran.emit_scene_text`` -- and is
named for the MASTER-PLAN section 3 row it proves:

    row 11  MeshStandardMaterial (PBR)     material standard objmat line
    row 13  Point / Spot lights            light point / light spot lines
    row 14  Fog                            fog linear / exp2 scene lines
    row 15  Textures / UV                  texture objmat line (PPM)
    row 16  Shadows                        shadow scene lines
    row 25  Tone mapping / colour space    tonemap scene lines

Plus the v1 stability contract: a plain ``cube`` scene emits exactly
the v1 .scene shape -- no Wave A lines at all.

Wave A end-to-end tests (seat B61): f3dc CLI + the real Fortran engine.

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/e2e/test_wavea_e2e.py

Like ``tests/e2e/test_cli.py``, every scene is driven in-process
through ``cli.main(["run", ...])`` into a ``tempfile`` tree and the
PPM is read back with ``tests/golden/check_image.py``.  Scenes render
at 160x120 (the golden regression is the exception: it is the
640x480 default by definition).  ``setUpClass`` follows test_cli's
pattern: the CLI's driver reuses an existing ``bin/engine3d`` as-is,
so when ``gfortran``+``make`` are available ``make`` runs once first
to keep the binary matched to the current sources; the suite skips
loudly only when no engine binary exists and none can be built.

Verified-render notes (160x120, this engine, 2026-11-23): the
engine's screen-space culling keeps the far-side faces of a cube
(the v1 convention behind the byte-identical golden), so the
point/spot tests place their lights on the far side of the cube,
where the visible faces actually receive diffuse light.

Scenes are SMALL (160x120 or 320x240) and stills only, except the

Wave C compiler parity tests (seat B83, MASTER-PLAN section 3).

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_wavec_parity.py

Mirrors the Wave B parity harness (``test_waveb_parity.py``): the
compile tests drive the real pipeline -- ``parser.parse`` ->
``validate.validate`` -> ``emit_fortran.emit_scene_text`` -- and are
named for the MASTER-PLAN section 3 row they prove:

    row 30  Post-processing     filter lines -> ordered post lines
                                (src/postprocess.f90, ext_post.py)
    row  3  Orthographic cam.   camera ortho -> ortho .scene line
                                (src/camera_ortho.f90, ext_cameras.py)
    row 22  True instancing     instance lines (scene.f90 appends a
                                copy of the source object)
    row 26  Multi-scene files   cli check/build split a 2-scene .f3d
                                into per-scene outputs

Three of the rows also carry a *rendered* assertion (gamma changes
pixels, ortho equalises sphere sizes, instances are visible), so --
unlike the pure-compile Wave B file -- this harness also renders
small scenes (320x240 stills) through ``cli.main(["run", ...])``
exactly like the e2e suites, reading PPMs back with
``tests/golden/check_image.py``.  ``make`` runs once (module level)
when gfortran+make are available so ``bin/engine3d`` matches the
current sources; the render tests skip loudly only when no engine
binary exists and none can be built.

Verified numbers on this tree (2026-11-23, 320x240): the ortho
sphere pair renders exactly 2764 red-dominant and 2764
blue-dominant pixels (perspective: 721 vs 4041); base cube alone
489 non-background pixels vs 1858 with its 3 instances.

Coverage (MASTER-PLAN section 3, Wave C):

    rows 30+3+22  examples/post-ortho.f3d end to end (the shipped
                  showcase: ortho camera, bloom/vignette/gamma chain,
                  instanced cube row, three depth spheres)
    row 26        examples/multi-scene.f3d run -> two distinct PPMs

Wave D compiler parity tests (seat D11, MASTER-PLAN row 7).

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_waved_parity.py
    python3 -m unittest tests.compiler.test_waved_parity

Mirrors the Wave C parity harness (``test_wavec_parity.py``): the
compile tests drive the real pipeline -- ``parser.parse`` ->
``validate.validate`` -> ``emit_fortran.emit_scene_text`` -- for each
of the eleven Wave D primitives (circle, ring, capsule, tube, lathe,
extrude, tetrahedron, octahedron, icosahedron, dodecahedron,
torusknot) and prove, per primitive:

  (a) the emitted ``.scene`` object line carries the right prim and
      the right dims mapping on the frozen 20-token line
      (SIZE / RADIUS / HEIGHT / SEGMENTS at tokens 17-20, 1-based):
      ring SIZE=inner / RADIUS=outer, torusknot SIZE=tube,
      extrude HEIGHT=depth (canonical prop ``extrude_depth``, the
      plain ``depth`` alias honoured), and the tube path triples /
      lathe + extrude point pairs appended as tokens 21+;
  (b) the validate triangle estimate for the compiled object equals
      the exact Fortran formula for that primitive (the formulas the
      ``geo_*_3d`` builders in ``src/geo_*.f90`` implement, owned on
      the compiler side by ``ext_geometry.estimate_triangles``);
  (c) the ring-repeat regression: ``ring 4 sphere`` still expands as
      the pre-existing repeat statement, while
      ``ring inner 0.5 outer 1`` is the ring primitive.

Token indices below are 0-based on the whitespace-split object line,
exactly as in ``tests/compiler/test_ext_geometry.py``.

Wave D end-to-end tests (seat D11): f3dc CLI + the real Fortran engine.

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/e2e/test_waved_e2e.py
    python3 -m unittest tests.e2e.test_waved_e2e

Mirrors ``tests/e2e/test_wavec_e2e.py``: scenes are driven in-process
through ``cli.main(["run", ...])`` into a ``tempfile`` tree and the
PPMs are read back with ``tests/golden/check_image.py``.
``setUpClass`` follows the Wave A/B/C pattern: ``make`` runs once
first (when gfortran+make are available) so ``bin/engine3d`` matches
the current sources; the suite skips loudly only when no engine
binary exists and none can be built.

Coverage (MASTER-PLAN row 7, Wave D geometries): a rendered PIXEL
PROOF per primitive family -- for each of the eleven new prims a
minimal single-object scene in a distinct saturated colour is built
and run through f3dc, and the test asserts the PPM exists, that more
than 300 non-background pixels belong to that prim's colour family,
and that the image is not flat (>= 3 distinct colours).  Plus the
shipped showcase ``examples/geometries.f3d`` end to end (>= 8
distinct dominant colours) and a determinism check (the showcase
rendered twice -> identical sha256).

Orientation notes (the known flat-prim trap): circle and ring are
flat discs in the XZ plane facing +Y (``src/geo_flat.f90``), so they
are rotated 90 degrees about X to face the camera head-on instead of
being seen edge-on.  A flat disc has a single face normal, hence a
single shade; those two scenes add a vignette filter, whose radial
falloff is what gives the disc its shading gradient (>= 3 distinct
colours).  Extrude footprints also lie in the XZ plane and grow
along +Y, so the extrude scene uses an elevated camera that sees
the top cap and two sides.

Wave E compiler parity tests (seat E11).

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_wavee_parity.py

Mirrors the Wave C / Wave D parity harnesses: the compile tests
drive the real pipeline -- ``parser.parse`` -> ``validate.validate``
-> ``emit_fortran.emit_scene_text`` (plus ``emit_json.emit_json_v2``
for the JSON payload) -- for the Wave E surface wired by the
coordinator:

* custom shaders: ``shader <name> expr "<expr>"`` definitions and
  the object prop ``shader <name>``, emitted as ``shaderdef`` /
  ``shaderbind`` .scene lines;
* skinning / morphs: ``morph <target> <kind> <factor>``,
  ``bone <name> [at x,y,z] [rotate rx,ry,rz] [radius r]`` and
  ``skin <target> <bonename>``, emitted as ``morph`` / ``bone`` /
  ``skin`` .scene lines (skins last);
* both ride in ``scene.extensions["wavee"]`` and into the v2 JSON
  payload.

The JS cross-checks shell out to ``node`` (skipped loudly via
``skipUnless`` when node is absent, the pattern from
``test_f3d_raycast_js.py``) and compare ``runtime/f3d-shader.js``
``evalRPN`` and ``runtime/f3d-skin.js`` ``morphApply`` /
``skinApply`` against independent Python reference implementations
of the same RPN / morph / skin semantics written below, within
1e-9 (factor-0 identity is exact).

NOTE on the checker RPN order (verified against the live compiler
on this tree, 2026-11-23): ``c * step(0.5, fract((x + y) * 2))``
compiles to ``c 0.5 x y + 2 * fract step *`` -- the leading ``c``
is the left operand of the outer ``*``, so it comes FIRST in RPN.
(The seat brief's example line listed the tokens in the order for
``step(...) * c`` instead; the tests below assert the line the
compiler actually emits, cross-checked token-for-token against
``ext_shader.to_rpn`` semantics and the JS evaluator grid.)

Wave E end-to-end tests (seat E12): f3dc CLI + the real Fortran engine.

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/e2e/test_wavee_e2e.py

Mirrors ``tests/e2e/test_wavec_e2e.py`` / ``test_waved_e2e.py``:
scenes are driven in-process through ``cli.main(["run", ...])``
into a ``tempfile`` tree and the PPMs are read back with
``tests/golden/check_image.py``.  ``setUpClass`` follows the
Wave A/B/C/D pattern: ``make`` runs once first (when gfortran+make
are available) so ``bin/engine3d`` matches the current sources;
the suite skips loudly only when no engine binary exists and none
can be built.

Coverage (Wave E: custom shaders, morph targets, skinning):

    shaders   a constant shader (``0.5``) renders every covered
              pixel exactly (128,128,128); shader ``c`` vs ``0``
              vs no shader are pairwise different, and ``0`` covers
              in pure black; the shipped checker expression yields
              exactly two covered colours, one of them black;
              shader ``c`` is byte-identical to ``material basic``
              (verified on this tree -- the strong form, not a
              centre-pixel approximation)
    morphs    factor 0 is a byte-identical identity on a sphere;
              bulge 1 changes both the hash and the covered-pixel
              count (on a cone -- see the note in
              test_morph_changes_render for why not a sphere)
    skinning  a zero-rotation bone is a byte-identical identity on
              a cylinder; a 30-degree bone bends it (hash differs)
    showcase  examples/wavee-showcase.f3d renders deterministically
              (two runs, identical sha256), with > 5000 non-bg
              pixels and >= 8 distinct colours
    golden    the no-arg legacy engine render is unchanged

Verified numbers on this tree (2026-11-23), all at 320x240 with
background (25, 25, 35) unless noted: the constant/checker/identity
cube scenes each cover 2757 pixels; the checker cube's covered
colours are exactly {(0,0,0), (220,60,60)}; the cone covers 1331
pixels plain and 2118 with ``morph s bulge 1``; the cylinder
covers 2692 pixels plain and 2543 skinned at 30 degrees; the
showcase (800x600, background (20,20,25)) covers 20031 non-bg
pixels with 397 distinct colours.

anim_cases.about: ANIM Wave 1 (ANIM-PLAN SS5.1) animation-compiler corpus: film mode, characters, built-in/custom actions, plain-word timelines (incl. plain-word<->numeric equivalence pairs with identical baked expectations), camera moves, dialogue/subtitles (incl. Bangla), multi-scene + transitions, loops & variables, fps/timebase edges, one minimal failing case per new diagnostic E206-E213/W203/W204 each with a near-miss valid twin, and the three SS1.10 example scripts. Expectations baked 2026-11-26 from the landed native bin/f3dc with the same extractor semantics as the corpus section of test_native_compiler.f90 (check capture sha256 + codes; build artifact sha256 sets, manifest excluded). Two cases bake landed-compiler defects against the plan (walks-in-from -> E201, gently -> E201) and one a limitation (let in repeat count), each named in the wave report. ANIM Wave 2 slice A1: case 152 re-pinned (E213 prints once -- carried item B fix in desugar let-substitution) and one case appended (character head triangle -> E205, carried item A: schema-driven character prop validation via the plugin registry). ANIM Wave 2 slice B1: timeline-artifact pins added to the 37 expectation cases (corpus/anim/examples/cli) whose builds now emit a .timeline.json -- in every case the ONLY delta, all other artifact hashes byte-identical -- plus six appended cases pinning the timeline artifact itself (film dialogue/camera, film two-scene cast union, Bangla dialogue, legacy keys, legacy verb, non-film character keys).
